requirements.text: The Framework must be capable of capturing information from the software tools specified in Table 3.9.3-A.
The user must be able to view the information in the central store in a hierarchical manner that makes sense to him.
The Framework must guard against malicious scripts on remote websites from accessing its information.
The Framework must guard against unintended corruption of information by the user himself.
The mean time between failures (MTBF) shall exceed 3 months.
Any coding conventions to be used during implementation must be documented before the beginning of the phase, and strictly adhered to during the phase.
The website for distributing the project shall include provisions for the users to make comments on the product as well as to compile a wish-list of features.
The system shall conform to ISO 10646 (Unicode UTF-8) and optionally ISO 10646-1 (Unicode UTF-16) standards for character set encoding.

The Framework shall implement a sandboxing mechanism or content security policy that prevents unauthorized execution of scripts or unauthorized access to the centralized data store by external applications.

The Framework shall implement an access control model (e.g., read-only modes, confirmation prompts for destructive actions, or versioning) to prevent accidental modification or deletion of information.
The system shall achieve an MTBF of 2,160 operational hours, where a failure is defined as any system crash or data corruption event requiring manual intervention to restore service.
The Framework shall implement sandboxing or process isolation for all third-party data ingestion modules to prevent arbitrary code execution from malicious web content.
The Framework shall implement ACID-compliant transactions for all data modifications to ensure data integrity and provide an undo mechanism for user-initiated operations.
The Framework shall respond to API queries for Entity retrieval within 200ms for a dataset of up to 10,000 Entities.
The total memory footprint of all ZNIX Framework background services shall not exceed 64MB of RAM under peak load.

OPEN: The PRD assumes that third-party applications are 'safe from vulnerabilities', which is a significant security risk. - The Framework shall implement input validation and sanitization for all data ingested from third-party applications to mitigate risks from potentially compromised or vulnerable software.

OPEN: The PRD lacks an upper bound on the volume of data or the number of entities the system is expected to manage. - The system shall support a minimum of 100,000 Entities and 10GB of total data storage while maintaining the specified performance constraints.

OPEN: The maximum supported number of Entities and Associates in the centralized store is not defined. - The Framework shall support a minimum of 100,000 Entities and 500,000 Associates without degradation in search performance.

OPEN: There is no requirement for the throughput of the data capturing mechanism. - The data capturing mechanism shall process and index at least 50 incoming email or document events per minute without blocking the client application.
